items.title: MVP launch & go/no-go
items.goal: The MVP is live on production by mid-December 2026, seeded with the fictional set, and stays reachable between review sessions despite Supabase Free pausing idle projects. Recruiters grade the AI against the quality bar, give structured feedback, and the team makes a documented go/no-go decision on moving to real data.
prd: Release plan → MVP: a working prototype of all capabilities on fictional data, live by mid-Dec 2026, ending with recruiter feedback sessions and a go/no-go decision → decided
AI governance → requirement 4: recruiters grade the AI on the sample set, English and Chinese separately → decided
Free-tier limits → Supabase Free pauses after a week idle; no backups; Hobby is non-commercial → decided
Open questions → what must be in place before real CVs are loaded; which paid plans; how backups work; the real-data date; the metric targets → open
Goals → the four success metrics apply from the real-data release, with targets set once Manatal baselines are exported → decided
exit: Production is deployed, seeded and reachable, with the re-seed runbook proven by an actual rebuild
The eval passes the bar for English and Chinese, or the shortfall is documented for the decision
Recruiter grading sessions are run and the feedback is captured in one place
The go/no-go pack is written and the decision is recorded with its date
outOfScope: Loading any real candidate data — that is what the decision is about
Buying paid plans or setting up backups before the decision — both are open questions
Migrating anything from Manatal — a non-goal
Success-metric targets, which are set once the Manatal baselines are exported

items.title: The MVP is live for recruiter sessions
items.story: As a recruiter invited to a review session, I want the portal to be up with believable data when I open it, so that the session is about the product rather than about why nothing loads.
ac: Given production, when it is deployed, then it runs in `sin1` against the production Supabase project with its migrations applied and the fictional set seeded.
Given a week between sessions, when nobody uses the portal, then the documented keep-alive procedure stops Supabase Free pausing it, or the restore procedure is known and takes minutes.
Given the release checklist, when it is run, then security, compliance, accessibility, the eval and the free-tier checks all have a recorded result before recruiters are invited.
prd: Environments & delivery → main deploys to production; migrations and seed files are the recovery plan → suggested
Free-tier limits → Supabase Free pauses after 1 week of inactivity; use it weekly or restore from the dashboard → decided
Free-tier limits → no backups; re-seed from the repo → decided
Non-functional requirements → uptime 99.5% on working days, best effort on free tiers → at risk

items.title: Deploy production and write the re-seed runbook
items.what: Take the MVP to production: apply migrations to the production Supabase project, seed the fictional set, verify the app in `sin1`, and write the runbook that rebuilds everything from migrations and seed — the MVP's only recovery plan, since there are no backups.
scope: Migrations applied to the production project with a recorded result
A production seed run, with its counts and cost recorded
`docs/runbooks/re-seed.md`: the exact steps, how long a rebuild takes, and what it costs in AI calls
A smoke check of the deployed app: dashboard, a job, a candidate and a search all load
Rollback: how to get back to a known state if a deploy goes wrong
exclusions: Buying a paid plan — an open question
done: Production is deployed in `sin1`, seeded, and the smoke check passes on all four screens
The re-seed runbook has been followed end to end at least once and records the real elapsed time and cost
The rollback procedure is written and names the exact commands
verify: production smoke check recorded in the runbook

items.title: Write the keep-alive and restore guidance for Supabase Free
items.what: Supabase Free pauses a project after a week of inactivity, which would take the MVP offline between review sessions. Document how to keep it awake within the free tier's limits and how to restore it quickly if it pauses anyway.
scope: A keep-alive approach that fits Vercel Hobby's once-a-day cron limit and Supabase Free's terms
`docs/runbooks/keep-alive.md`: what runs, how often, who checks it, and how to tell whether the project is paused
Restore: the exact steps and how long it takes from the dashboard
A note that this is a free-tier workaround that disappears on a paid plan
exclusions: Anything that breaks Supabase's or Vercel's terms
done: The keep-alive approach is documented, stays within both providers' free-tier terms, and names who checks it
The restore procedure is written with its expected duration
The runbook states what changes on a paid plan
verify: cron configuration, if any, respects the once-a-day limit

items.title: Run the release readiness check before recruiter sessions
items.what: Before recruiters are invited, run one consolidated readiness check across security, compliance, accessibility, the quality bar, performance targets and the free-tier position, and record the result — including anything that is knowingly not ready.
scope: `docs/runbooks/release-readiness.md` with a checklist and a recorded result per item
Security: the `security-check` list, including the no-secret-in-bundle and RLS lock-down evidence
Compliance: the fairness review's findings closed or accepted
Accessibility and responsiveness: the standard's checks passing at both widths
Quality: the eval result for English and Chinese, with any shortfall stated plainly
Performance: CV parse under 30 seconds and search under 3 seconds, with measured figures
Free tier: the Hobby non-commercial position restated as an open decision
exclusions: Fixing what the check finds — those become issues
done: Every checklist item has a recorded result with its evidence, including measured parse and search times
Anything not ready is listed explicitly rather than omitted, with an issue raised
The eval figures for English and Chinese are recorded even if one is below the bar

items.title: Recruiters grade the AI and give structured feedback
items.story: As a recruiter in a review session, I want a clear way to say where the AI helped and where it got things wrong, so that the go/no-go decision reflects what using it is actually like.
ac: Given a grading session, when it is run, then recruiters grade parsed fields and top-5 rankings against the same bar the eval uses, with English and Chinese sessions kept separate.
Given feedback, when it is captured, then it is recorded in one place, attributable to the session rather than to an individual's memory.
Given a disagreement between a recruiter and the answer key, when it is recorded, then the key is corrected rather than the recruiter overruled.
prd: AI governance → requirement 4: recruiters grade the AI on the sample set against the quality bar, English and Chinese separately → decided
Release plan → the MVP ends with recruiter feedback sessions and a go/no-go decision → decided

items.title: Write the grading session guide and the feedback capture template
items.what: Prepare the recruiter sessions: a guide for running them, the tasks recruiters work through, and a template that captures grading and free-text feedback in a form that feeds both the answer key and the go/no-go pack.
scope: `docs/sessions/grading-guide.md`: how a session runs, how long it takes, what recruiters are asked to do
Separate English and Chinese grading passes, scored against the same bar
A capture template covering parsed-field correctness, top-5 agreement, and free-text observations
How a recruiter's disagreement with the answer key is routed back into correcting the key
A note that no real candidate data is used in any session
exclusions: Running the sessions — recruiters and the product owner do that
Collecting personal data from recruiters beyond their name
done: The guide covers a complete session end to end, including who does what and how long it takes
The template captures field correctness, top-5 agreement and free text, split by language
The route from recruiter disagreement to a corrected answer key is written down
The guide states that only fictional data is used
verify: the template's fields match the eval's scoring rules

items.title: The team makes a documented go/no-go decision
items.story: As the product owner, I want one pack that says what the MVP proved, what it cost, what is still open and what real data would require, so that the decision is made on evidence and recorded for whoever asks later.
ac: Given the pack, when it is read, then it states the eval results for English and Chinese, the recruiter feedback, and the performance and cost figures measured in the MVP.
Given the six open questions, when the pack is read, then each one is listed with what it blocks and who must answer it.
Given a go decision, when it is recorded, then the real-data prerequisites are listed as the next release's entry conditions.
prd: Release plan → the MVP ends with a go/no-go decision; the real-data release has no date and depends on the MVP outcome → decided
Open questions → all six, including what must be in place before real CVs are loaded → open
Data, privacy & compliance → Risk 1: loading real CVs without sign-in would breach PDPA's Protection Obligation → decided
Goals → success metrics apply from the real-data release, targets set once Manatal baselines are exported → decided

items.title: Assemble the go/no-go pack and record the decision
items.what: Bring the evidence together into one pack the product owner can decide from: quality results by language, recruiter feedback, measured performance and cost, the open questions, and what loading real data would require — then record the decision and its date.
scope: `docs/go-no-go/pack.md`: eval results for English and Chinese, recruiter feedback themes, measured parse and search times, and the MVP's actual AI cost
The six PRD open questions, each with what it blocks and who must answer
Real-data prerequisites, led by the PDPA protection problem that no sign-in creates, drawn from the compliance baseline
A decision record with the date, the decision, and the conditions attached to it
Whatever is still unknown stated as unknown rather than estimated
exclusions: Making the decision — the product owner does that
Settling any of the six open questions
Starting real-data work before the decision
done: The pack states the English and Chinese eval results, the feedback themes and the measured performance and cost figures
All six open questions appear with what each blocks and who must answer
The real-data prerequisites are listed, with the no-sign-in PDPA risk first
The decision, its date and its conditions are recorded once the product owner decides
verify: every figure in the pack cites the run or report it came from
